newsitem.title: GEORGIA: SOCCER-DYNAMO TBILISI WIN SIXTH SUCCESSIVE DOUBLE. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DYNAMO TBILISI WIN SIXTH SUCCESSIVE DOUBLE. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: Georgia's Dynamo Tbilisi completed their sixth successive league and cup double on Monday with a 1-0 Cup final win over Dynamo Batumi from the Black Sea region of Adzharia. (Corrects location)

A powerful 30th-minute strike from club top scorer Georgy Demetradze clinched it for Tbilisi, who have also taken an unbeatable lead over Batumi in the league to maintain a 100 percent record -- they have won all eight championships since Georgian soccer broke away from the Soviet league in 1990.

All too open to creeping complacency at home, the 1981 European Cup Winners' Cup champions have their sights firmly set on Europe next season, though the departure of top players to the West -- including Manchester City's $3-million midfielder Georgi Kinkladze -- has hampered their progress in recent years.
"The international scene is the main thing for us," Tbilisi coach Nodar Akobia said. The club will go into the Champions' League hoping to do better than last season's second-round UEFA Cup exit.
It is not just the lack of domestic competition that drives the club's hunger for European exposure.

Scarred by civil wars in Abkhazia and elsewhere and plunged into desperate poverty by the collapse of communism, Georgians still cherish memories of Dynamo Tbilisi's European triumph when they beat Liverpool on the way to lifting the Cup.
